content.text:
I added the `version` subcommand. `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` both pass.

- **`internal/cmds/version.go`** (new): `Version(args []string) error` reports the app name `"app"`, `BuildVersion` (default `"dev"`) and `runtime.Version()`. Set the version at build time with `-ldflags "-X example.com/app/internal/cmds.BuildVersion=1.2.3"`.
- **`internal/cmds/registry.go`**: registered `{"version", "show the version", Version}` at the end of `All`.
- **`internal/cmds/version_test.go`** (new): table-driven tests for the report fields, `Version` with and without extra args, the default version, and the registration.

- **Output goes to stderr as a log record.** The existing commands use `fmt.Printf`, but the project rules say nothing under `internal/` prints. So `Version` logs through `internal/log` as `name=app version=dev go=...`. The `Run` signature has no writer to print to. If you want it on stdout instead, `Run` would need an `io.Writer`, which means changing every command and `main`.
- **One package-level variable.** `BuildVersion` has to be a package-level `var`, because `-ldflags -X` can only set one. It conflicts with the no-mutable-state rule, and it is documented in the code.
- **Tests don't check the logged text.** They check the field-building helper and that `Version` returns nil, since the logger writes straight to stderr.
